mainTopic: Slaughtering the קרבן פסח for people whose eating is uncertain, and the dispute of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי over slaughtering it for a single person.
overview: The משנה lists people who might not be able to eat the קרבן פסח at night: one clearing rubble, a prisoner promised release, and the sick and elderly. The פסח may be slaughtered for them as part of a group, but not for them alone. If something later goes wrong, they are exempt from פסח שני, except the rubble-clearer who was טמא from the start. The גמרא limits the prisoner rule twice. רבי יוחנן says a promise from a Jewish prison can be trusted. רב חסדא says a prison inside the wall of בית פאגי is also fine, because the meat can be brought to him there. רבי יוחנן also limits the rubble-clearer's obligation to a round pile, and a ברייתא confirms this. A new משנה brings a dispute: רבי יהודה forbids slaughtering a פסח for a יחיד, while רבי יוסי permits it if he can eat. The גמרא explains how each reads the verse ״בְּאַחַד״, including רבי שמעון's private-altar law. Finally, רב עוקבא challenges רבי יהודה from a ברייתא about a woman. רבא answers that a group of only women is allowed, and only mixed groups of women, slaves, and minors are forbidden. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: People whose eating is uncertain can still have the פסח slaughtered for them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the קרבן פסח may be slaughtered for the person clearing rubble, a prisoner promised release, and a sick or elderly person who can eat a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who is clearing away a pile of rubble, and likewise someone who was promised release from prison, and a sick person or an elderly person who are able to eat an olive-sized amount: we slaughter the פסח on their behalf.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists four kinds of people who may not manage to eat the פסח tonight. It rules that we may still slaughter it for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these people is fit right now, at the time of slaughter, but something could go wrong later. The rubble-clearer might find a dead body and become טמא. The prisoner might not actually be released. The sick or elderly person might become too weak to eat. Since they are fit now, the slaughter is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who clears away a pile of rubble to search for a buried person
Prison
An olive-sized amount, the minimum measure for eating
We slaughter the קרבן on their behalf

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the beginning of the משנה. The list is continuing from earlier cases on the previous part of the דף, which is why it opens with 'and'.

phrases.english: And one who clears away the pile of rubble,
phrases.notes: Searching for someone buried underneath. If that person is dead, the searcher becomes טמא מת.

phrases.english: and likewise one whom they promised
to release him from prison,
phrases.notes: Promised release in time for the night of פסח.

phrases.english: and the sick person and the elderly person
who are able to eat an olive-bulk
phrases.notes: Able right now, at the time of slaughter.

phrases.english: one slaughters the Pesach on their behalf.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַמְפַקֵּחַ אֶת הַגַּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list from the earlier part of the משנה, on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who are fit now but might not be able to eat later may have the פסח slaughtered for them.

steps.title: But not for them alone
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the previous rule: the פסח may not be slaughtered for these people by themselves, in case it ends up uneaten and becomes פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all of them, we do not slaughter on their behalf by themselves, because perhaps they will cause the פסח to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit. These people must be part of a group that also includes people who will definitely be able to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'By themselves' means either as an individual, or in a group made up only of such uncertain people. If they all turn out unable to eat, nobody eats the קרבן, and it becomes פסול. Having a fully fit person in the group protects the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: By themselves, without fully fit people in the group
Perhaps, out of concern that
To a state of disqualification

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not take back step 1. Step 1 says these people can be included in a slaughter. Step 2 only says they cannot be the only ones it is slaughtered for.

phrases.english: For all of them, one does not slaughter on their behalf
by themselves,
phrases.notes: Alone, or in a group made up entirely of such people.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא יָבִיאוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח לִידֵי פְסוּל.
phrases.english: lest they bring the Pesach to disqualification.
phrases.notes: A פסח with no one able to eat it is פסול.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כּוּלָּם אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין עֲלֵיהֶן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח may not be slaughtered for uncertain people alone, because of the risk that it becomes פסול.

steps.title: Exempt from פסח שני, except the rubble-clearer
steps.stepSummary: Because the slaughter was valid for them, these people are exempt from פסח שני even if a problem comes up later. The exception is the rubble-clearer who was טמא from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, if a disqualification happened to them, they are exempt from bringing פסח שני, except for the one clearing the pile, because he was impure from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens if one of these people ends up unable to eat. They do not need to bring פסח שני, with one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters for פסח שני is whether the פסח was validly slaughtered for you, not whether you actually ate it. Since these people were fit at the time of slaughter, they are covered. The rubble-clearer who finds a dead body is different. He was already standing over the corpse before the slaughter, so he was never fit, and he must bring פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
The second פסח, brought a month later by those who missed the first
Exempt
Impure from the very beginning

steps.whatToRemember: The obligation of פסח שני depends on whether the slaughter was valid for you at the time, not on whether you got to eat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key principle: fitness at the time of slaughter is what counts.

phrases.english: Therefore, if a disqualification happened to them
they are exempt from making the second Pesach,
except for the one clearing the pile,
phrases.notes: When the buried person is found dead.

phrases.english: for he was impure from the start.
phrases.notes: He was already over the corpse before the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אֵירַע בָּהֶן פְּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence ('therefore') from the slaughter being valid for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They are exempt from פסח שני, except the rubble-clearer, who was טמא from the outset.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the prisoner rule to a non-Jewish prison
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר הונא quotes רבי יוחנן: the משנה's ban on slaughtering for a prisoner alone applies only to a non-Jewish prison. For a Jewish prison, we may slaughter for him alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבה בר הונא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only about a non-Jewish prison. But in a Jewish prison, we slaughter for him even by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבי יוחנן narrows the משנה's rule about the prisoner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה put all four people in one category, all needing a group. רבי יוחנן says that the prisoner is an exception when the prison is Jewish. In that case, he may have the פסח slaughtered for him alone. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about, a formula for limiting a rule
Of a non-Jew
Of Jews

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabba bar Huna said Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין דְּגוֹי,
phrases.english: They taught this only for a prison belonging to non-Jews,
phrases.notes: He's talking about the rule from step 2, as it applies to the prisoner.

phrases.english: but a prison belonging to Jews —
one slaughters for him even by himself,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין דְּגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's 'not by themselves' rule for the prisoner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a prisoner in a Jewish prison, the פסח may be slaughtered even for him alone.

steps.title: Why we trust a Jewish promise
steps.stepSummary: Jewish authorities who promised release will keep their word, as the פסוק in צפניה says that the remnant of Israel does not speak lies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they promised him, they will release him, as it is written: 'The remnant of Israel will not do iniquity nor speak lies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רבי יוחנן's ruling and backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a Jewish prison, the promise of release is treated as certain, so there is no real doubt that the prisoner will be able to eat. A non-Jewish authority's promise is not given this trust. The פסוק from צפניה is the source for assuming that Jews keep their word.

keyTerms.meaning: Since they promised him
They will release him
As it is written
A lie

steps.whatToRemember: The prisoner needs a group only when there is real doubt about his release. A Jewish authority's promise removes that doubt.

phrases.english: since they promised him, they will release him,
as it is written: 'The remnant of Israel will not do iniquity
nor speak lies.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאַבְטְחִינְהוּ, מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason and scriptural support for step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a prisoner in a Jewish prison may have the פסח slaughtered for him alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: צפניה 3:13: 'שארית ישראל לא יעשו עולה ולא ידברו כזב'

steps.title: A prison inside the wall of בית פאגי counts differently
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the rule about a non-Jewish prison. The ban on slaughtering for the prisoner alone applies only when the prison is outside the wall of בית פאגי. Inside that wall, we may slaughter for him alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What you said about a non-Jewish prison only applies if the prison is outside the wall of בית פאגי. If it is inside that wall, we may slaughter the פסח for him alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a second limit to the ban on slaughtering the פסח for a prisoner alone. Even in a non-Jewish prison, the ban only applies if the prison is outside the area where the פסח may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, רבי יוחנן said the ban applies only to a non-Jewish prison. רב חסדא now narrows it further, based on where the prison is located. The wall of בית פאגי marks the area in which the פסח may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Prison
The wall of בית פאגי, the outer boundary inside which the פסח may be eaten
By himself, alone
We only said this when, a formula that introduces a limit on a rule

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
That which you said, about a prison belonging to non-Jews,
phrases.notes: This refers back to רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 4.

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא חוּץ לְחוֹמַת בֵּית פָּאגֵי.
phrases.english: we only said this when it is outside the wall of Beit Pagei.
But if it is inside the wall of Beit Pagei,
we slaughter on his behalf even by himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit to רבי יוחנן's rule about a non-Jewish prison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A prisoner held in a non-Jewish prison inside the wall of בית פאגי may have the פסח slaughtered for him alone.

steps.title: Why: his portion can be brought to him
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that even if he stays in prison, people can bring him his share of the פסח, and he can eat it there.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because it is possible to bring him the meat, and he will eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב חסדא's rule. Since the prison is inside the area where the פסח may be eaten, his share can be carried to him in prison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original worry was that the פסח would go uneaten and become פסול. Here that worry falls away, because he can eat it even without being released. So it no longer matters whether the non-Jews keep their promise.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
They bring it to him

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is possible for them to bring it to him, and he will eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא — אֶפְשָׁר דְּאַמְטוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב חסדא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's permission to slaughter for a prisoner held inside the wall of בית פאגי
steps.raayaSupportSource: Practical logic: the meat can be carried to him in prison, so there is no danger that it goes uneaten.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on slaughtering for a prisoner alone exists only because the meat might go uneaten. Whenever he is sure to eat it (a Jewish prison, or a prison inside בית פאגי), we may slaughter for him alone.

steps.title: The rubble-clearer brings a פסח שני only for a round pile
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: the משנה's ruling that the rubble-clearer brings a פסח שני applies only to a round pile. For a long pile he is exempt, because perhaps he was still טהור when the פסח was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Therefore, if something happened…' רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only about a round pile. But with a long pile, he is exempt from פסח שני, because we can say he was טהור at the time of the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exception about the rubble-clearer and limits it. Only with a round pile is it certain that he became טמא before the פסח was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A round pile is compact, so whoever works on it certainly stood over the dead body at some point before the פסח was slaughtered. A long pile is spread out, so he may still have been working at the far end when the פסח was slaughtered. Since it is a doubt, he keeps his valid פסח and is exempt from פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore, if something happened. These are the opening words of the משנה being discussed
A round pile of rubble
A long pile of rubble
The second פסח, brought a month later by those who missed the first
At the time of the slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: He is not declared definitely טהור. Since we simply do not know when he became טמא, we can say he was still טהור at the slaughter, and the valid slaughter stands.

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah: 'Therefore, if it occurred, etc.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the line in the משנה it is about to explain.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
They taught this only about a round pile.
But with a long pile,
he is exempt from bringing a second Pesach,
because one can say: he was pure at the time of the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אֵירַע וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא גַּל עָגוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the prisoner to the next line of the משנה, the rubble-clearer, and limits its exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only someone clearing a round pile must bring a פסח שני. Someone clearing a long pile is exempt because of the doubt.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the round-pile and long-pile distinction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי שמעון בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה teaches the same distinction. A round pile obligates him in פסח שני, and a long pile exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: רבי שמעון, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: Someone clearing a pile is sometimes exempt and sometimes obligated. How so? If it was a round pile and טומאה was found under it, he is obligated. If it was a long pile and טומאה was found under it, he is exempt, because we can say he was טהור at the time of the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יוחנן said. This backs up his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the same two cases and the same reason ('we can say he was טהור at the slaughter'). This shows that רבי יוחנן's distinction is an older teaching and not his own new idea.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught in a ברייתא this way. A formula that introduces support
One who clears away a pile of rubble
Sometimes exempt, sometimes obligated
Ritual impurity, here a dead body

steps.whatToRemember: The rubble-clearer brings a פסח שני only when it is certain he was טמא at the slaughter (a round pile). If it is doubtful (a long pile), his original פסח counts.

phrases.english: This was also taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
One who clears a pile of rubble
is sometimes exempt and sometimes obligated.
How so?

phrases.aramaic: גַּל עָגוֹל וְנִמְצֵאת טוּמְאָה תַּחְתָּיו — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: If it was a round pile and impurity was found under it, he is obligated.

phrases.aramaic: גַּל אָרוֹךְ וְנִמְצֵאת טוּמְאָה תַּחְתָּיו — פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: If it was a long pile and impurity was found under it, he is exempt,
because one can say he was pure at the time of the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's ruling with a matching ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's distinction between a round pile and a long pile
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה

steps.title: New משנה: may the Pesach be slaughtered for one person?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי יהודה rules that the פסח may not be slaughtered for one person alone. רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not slaughter the פסח for an individual. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a dispute. The question is whether a פסח may be slaughtered for a single person, or only for a group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה requires a group to share the פסח. רבי יוסי allows even one person to bring it alone. The גמרא will later explain the source of each view.

keyTerms.meaning: Abbreviation for מתניתין, our משנה
An individual, one person alone
Permits

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד —
phrases.english: We do not slaughter the Pesach on behalf of an individual;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And Rabbi Yosei permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of the previous one ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה forbids slaughtering the פסח for one person alone. רבי יוסי permits it.

steps.title: No slaughter for a group that cannot eat a כזית
steps.stepSummary: Even a large group of one hundred people may not have the פסח slaughtered for them if, together, they cannot eat a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even a group of one hundred people who cannot eat a כזית: we do not slaughter for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule. The size of the group does not help if none of its members can eat a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key requirement is the ability to eat the פסח, not the number of people. Even רבי יהודה, who requires a group, agrees that a big group is worthless if they cannot eat. This fits the earlier rule (Step 1) that a sick or elderly person must be able to eat a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: A group registered together for one פסח
An olive's volume, the minimum amount of eating that counts

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the פסח is fundamentally tied to being eaten. A slaughter for people who cannot eat it has no purpose.

phrases.english: And even a group of one hundred
who are unable to eat an olive-bulk,
we do not slaughter on their behalf.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ חֲבוּרָה שֶׁל מֵאָה שֶׁאֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לֶאֱכוֹל כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the new משנה with a related rule about who may have the פסח slaughtered for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A group that cannot eat a כזית may not have the פסח slaughtered for them, no matter how large it is.

steps.title: No group made of women, slaves, and minors
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with one more rule: a פסח group is not formed from נשים, עבדים, and קטנים together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not make a group for the פסח made up of women, slaves, and minors.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It adds one more rule about who may form a group for the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10 and 11 dealt with how many people a פסח may be slaughtered for and whether they can eat it. This line deals with what kind of people make up the group. The משנה rules out a group made of this mix of people.

keyTerms.meaning: A group registered together to share one קרבן פסח
Women
Canaanite slaves
Minors, children under בר/בת מצוה age

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is a group made of this mix of people together. Do not assume each of these people is barred from the פסח. The גמרא later explains the reason and which groupings are allowed.

phrases.english: And we do not make a group
of women, slaves, and minors.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין חֲבוּרַת נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of rules about forming a פסח group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח group may not be made up of women, slaves, and minors together.

steps.title: The verse behind רבי יהודה's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. It shows that רבי יהודה learns from the word ״בְּאַחַד״ that a פסח is not slaughtered for a יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Sages taught in a ברייתא: From where do we know that we do not slaughter the פסח for one person alone? The verse says: 'You may not sacrifice the פסח in one (בְּאַחַד).' These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It brings a ברייתא that gives the Torah source for רבי יהודה's view from the משנה (step 10).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads ״בְּאַחַד״ as 'for one person.' The verse then means a פסח may not be slaughtered for a single person. This gives a verse-based reason for his ruling in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that follows the משנה
'The Sages taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
'From where do we know?' A request for a source.
'The verse teaches.' This introduces the verse used as a source.
A single individual

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
From where do we know that we do not slaughter
the Paschal lamb for an individual?
The verse states:
'You may not sacrifice the Paschal lamb in one'
phrases.notes: Deuteronomy 16:5. רבי יהודה reads 'in one' as 'for one person.'

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by giving the Torah source for רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's rule that a פסח is not slaughtered for a יחיד
steps.raayaSupportSource: Deuteronomy 16:5, ״לֹא תוּכַל לִזְבֹּחַ אֶת הַפָּסַח בְּאַחַד״, read as 'for one person'

steps.title: רבי יוסי: what matters is the ability to eat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that one person who can eat the פסח may have it slaughtered for him. Ten people who cannot eat it may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי says: One person who is able to eat it, we slaughter for him. Ten people who are not able to eat it, we do not slaughter for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי's opposing view. For him, the number of people does not matter. Only their ability to eat the פסח does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's test is how many people there are. רבי יוסי's test is whether they can eat at least a כזית. This matches step 11, where even a large group is not enough if no one can eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Able to eat it, meaning at least a כזית of the פסח
We slaughter on his behalf
Ten people

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei says:
An individual who is able to eat it,
we slaughter on his behalf;
ten who are unable to eat it,
we do not slaughter on their behalf.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: יָחִיד וְיָכוֹל לְאׇכְלוֹ שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The test for slaughtering a פסח is whether the people can eat it, not how many people there are.

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי use the word ״בְּאַחַד״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי learns from the word ״בְּאַחַד״, since he does not read it the way רבי יהודה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי, what does he do with this word 'in one'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. If רבי יוסי does not learn רבי יהודה's rule from ״בְּאַחַד״, what does that word teach him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that every word of the Torah teaches something. רבי יוסי rejected רבי יהודה's reading, so he must use ״בְּאַחַד״ for something else. The גמרא now wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does he do with it?' That is, what does he learn from this verse?
'In one.' The key word in the verse.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei, this word 'in one,'
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, הַאי ״בְּאַחַד״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי יוסי reads the verse that רבי יהודה used as his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוסי learns from the word ״בְּאַחַד״

steps.title: He uses it for רבי שמעון's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי יוסי needs ״בְּאַחַד״ for a teaching of רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in short: רבי יוסי uses the word for a different law, the one taught by רבי שמעון. This line sets up the next step, which quotes רבי שמעון's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word is already used for another law, it is not available to teach רבי יהודה's rule. That is why רבי יוסי can disagree with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needs it.' The verse is already used for a different teaching.
For the teaching of רבי שמעון

phrases.english: He needs it for that which Rabbi Shimon taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי uses ״בְּאַחַד״ for רבי שמעון's teaching, not for the rule against slaughtering for a יחיד.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a פסח on a private altar is a לא תעשה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון. Offering a פסח on a בָּמַת יָחִיד when private altars are forbidden breaks a לא תעשה, learned from ״בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says: From where do we know that one who offers his פסח on a private altar, at a time when private altars are forbidden, breaks a negative commandment? The verse says: 'You may not sacrifice the פסח in one of your gates.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's teaching in full. This shows the other law that רבי יוסי learns from ״בְּאַחַד״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads 'in one of your gates' as 'in any local spot,' meaning a private altar. The verse is then a לא תעשה against offering a פסח there. The verse is used up for this law, which is why רבי יוסי does not learn רבי יהודה's rule from it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught in a ברייתא'
A private, improvised altar
A period when private altars were forbidden, because there was a central place of worship
A negative commandment
'Your gates,' meaning your local towns

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read the same verse differently. רבי יהודה stresses 'one' as one person. רבי שמעון reads 'one of your gates' as a local place, meaning a private altar.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
From where do we know that one who sacrifices his Paschal lamb
on a private altar
at a time when private altars are prohibited
is in violation of a negative commandment?
The verse states:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תוּכַל לִזְבֹּחַ אֶת הַפָּסַח בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: 'You may not sacrifice the Paschal lamb in one of your gates.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִין לַזּוֹבֵחַ אֶת פִּסְחוֹ בְּבָמַת יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the ברייתא that step 16 referred to.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יוסי uses ״בְּאַחַד״ for another law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון, which learns from ״בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ״ a לא תעשה against offering a פסח on a בָּמַת יָחִיד

steps.title: The prohibition applies only when everyone uses one central altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rejects the idea that the prohibition applies even when private altars are permitted. It applies only when all of Israel goes to 'one gate,' the central altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might have thought this is so even at a time when private altars are permitted. So the verse says 'in one of your gates.' They said this only at a time when all of Israel enters through one gate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון raises a possible mistake: maybe the prohibition applies even when private altars are allowed. He uses the verse's wording to reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'one … gate' hints at a time when all of Israel gathers at one central place, such as the בית המקדש. So the לא תעשה applies only in such a period. When private altars are permitted, a פסח may be offered on one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I might have thought.' This introduces a possible mistaken idea.
A period when private altars were permitted
'One gate,' meaning a single central place of worship for all of Israel

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns from ״בְּאַחַד״ that a פסח is not slaughtered for a יחיד. רבי יוסי judges by whether the people can eat it. He uses ״בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ״ for רבי שמעון's law: a פסח on a private altar is a לא תעשה, but only when all of Israel goes to one central altar.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף בִּשְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר הַבָּמוֹת כֵּן,
phrases.english: I might have thought that even at a time when private altars are permitted, this is so;
therefore the verse states: 'in one of your gates,'
they said this only at a time
when all of Israel enters through one gate.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף בִּשְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר הַבָּמוֹת כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the prohibition just taught in step 17 to times when private altars are forbidden.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that offering a פסח on a בָּמַת יָחִיד is forbidden even when private altars are permitted
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse's words 'one … gate' limit the prohibition to a time when all of Israel worships at one central altar.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn the private-altar law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns רבי שמעון's rule about private altars, since he already used ״בְּאַחַד״ for his own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, where does he learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רבי יהודה. He used ״בְּאַחַד״ to teach that we do not slaughter a פסח for one person, so where does he get רבי שמעון's rule about private altars?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw that רבי יוסי uses ״בְּאַחַד״ for רבי שמעון's teaching about a בָּמַת יָחִיד. רבי יהודה already used the same word for a different law. So the גמרא wants to know whether רבי יהודה has any source for the private-altar prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it? What is his source?
This (law)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda,
from where does he derive this?
phrases.notes: 'This' means רבי שמעון's rule about bringing a פסח on a private altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the source question around. Steps 15 to 18 asked about רבי יוסי, and now the same question is asked about רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי יהודה's source for the prohibition of a פסח on a private altar?

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns two lessons from one verse
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רבי יהודה learns both laws from ״בְּאַחַד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: You learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה takes both laws from the same verse. One law is no פסח for one person, and the other is no פסח on a private altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not need two separate verses. He reads ״בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ״ as carrying two lessons at once.

keyTerms.meaning: You learn two things from it (one verse teaches two laws)

phrases.english: You learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְתֵּי שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns both the 'not for one person' rule and the private-altar rule from ״בְּאַחַד״.

steps.title: Why should רבי יוסי not read the verse like רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי knows that ״בְּאַחַד״ teaches רבי שמעון's rule and not רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יוסי, how do we know the verse teaches what רבי שמעון said? Maybe it comes to teach what רבי יהודה said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי. Maybe ״בְּאַחַד״ really does mean 'not for one person,' as רבי יהודה says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse could teach רבי יהודה's rule, then רבי יוסי's ruling would be in danger. He allows slaughtering the פסח for one person who can eat it. So the גמרא wants to know why רבי יוסי is sure the verse is about private altars.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
Perhaps, maybe
That it comes (to teach)

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Yosei,
from where do we know it is for this, which Rabbi Shimon said?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא כִּדְקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דַּאֲתָא?
phrases.english: Perhaps it comes to teach what Rabbi Yehuda said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, מִמַּאי דִּלְהָכִי דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוסי's reading from step 16 and tests it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's choice to read ״בְּאַחַד״ like רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse could just as easily mean 'not for one person,' which would go against רבי יוסי's ruling.

steps.title: Another verse shows a פסח can be for one person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that ״אִישׁ לְפִי אׇכְלוֹ״ shows a פסח can be slaughtered for one man, so ״בְּאַחַד״ cannot mean the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: You cannot think that, because it is written: ״אִישׁ לְפִי אׇכְלוֹ״, 'each man according to his eating.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוסי. The Torah says ״אִישׁ״, one man, so a פסח can be slaughtered for one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since another verse already allows a פסח for one person, ״בְּאַחַד״ cannot be forbidding that. So רבי יוסי reads ״בְּאַחַד״ as רבי שמעון's private-altar rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible
'Each man according to his eating' (שמות יב:ד)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: ״בְּאַחַד״ teaches both 'no פסח for one person' and 'no private altar.' רבי יוסי: ״אִישׁ לְפִי אׇכְלוֹ״ allows a פסח for one person, so ״בְּאַחַד״ teaches only the private-altar rule.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
This cannot enter your mind,
because it is written: 'Each man according to his eating.'
phrases.notes: The singular word 'man' shows that one person is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a second verse that rules out the other reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״בְּאַחַד״ might forbid slaughtering a פסח for one person.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אִישׁ לְפִי אׇכְלוֹ״ allows a פסח for one person, so ״בְּאַחַד״ must teach רבי שמעון's rule.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to show רבי יהודה allows a פסח for one woman
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חיננא challenges רבא. A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה as allowing a פסח to be slaughtered for a woman by herself on the first פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חיננא from Perishna raised a contradiction to רבא: Did רבי יהודה really say we do not slaughter the פסח for one person? But a ברייתא says: For a woman on the first פסח, we slaughter for her by herself. On the second פסח, we make her part of other people's group. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רב עוקבא points out that רבי יהודה seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says no פסח for one person. In this ברייתא, he allows a פסח for one woman 'by herself' on the first פסח. On פסח שני, she may only join others. The two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him
And we raise a contradiction (between two sources)
For a single person
Secondary; joined onto others, not on her own

steps.confusionAlert: 'הָרִאשׁוֹן' and 'הַשֵּׁנִי' here mean the first פסח (14 ניסן) and פסח שני (14 אייר). They do not mean a first and second woman.

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חִינָּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Chinana raised a contradiction
(he was) from Perishna, to Rava:
Did Rabbi Yehuda say

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד?
phrases.english: we do not slaughter the Pesach for an individual?
But raise a contradiction:
A woman, on the first (Pesach),
we slaughter for her by herself,
and on the second (Pesach) we make her secondary to others,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חִינָּנָא מִפָּרִישְׁנָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רבי יהודה's basic rule in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has רבי יהודה allowing slaughter for a woman by herself, which seems to contradict his own rule.

steps.title: רבא: read it as 'women by themselves'
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes the wording of the ברייתא. It means a group of women on their own, not one woman alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do not say 'by herself.' Rather, say 'by themselves.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by changing one word in the ברייתא. It refers to a group of women, not a single woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this change, the ברייתא never allows a פסח for one person. It only allows a group made up of women alone, so רבי יהודה's rule stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say this; rather, say that (a change in the wording)
By themselves (plural, a group)

phrases.english: He said to him:
Do not say 'by herself,'
rather say: 'by themselves.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ, אֶלָּא אֵימָא: בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows a פסח for one woman alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows a group made up only of women.

steps.title: Can a group be made up only of women?
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא challenges רבא from a משנה that seems to forbid groups of only women, only slaves, or only minors.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do we make a group of only women? But we learned in a משנה: We do not make a group of women, slaves, and minors. Doesn't that mean women alone, slaves alone, and minors alone?
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוקבא attacks רבא's answer. A משנה seems to forbid exactly the all-women group that רבא just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה means no group of only women, then רבא's new wording is not allowed either. The question is how to read the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: A group registered together on one קרבן פסח
But we learned in a משנה
Is it not that...? (suggesting a reading)
By themselves, alone

phrases.english: He said to him:
Do we make a group that is all women?
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹשִׂין חֲבוּרַת נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים,
phrases.english: We do not make a group of women, slaves, and minors,
is it not (referring to)
women by themselves,
and slaves by themselves, and minors by themselves?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי עָבְדִינַן חֲבוּרָה שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's new reading: a group of women by themselves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה seems to forbid a group made up of only one of these types, including only women.

steps.title: The משנה only forbids mixed groups
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה forbids groups that mix women, slaves, and minors, and begins to give the reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. It means women, slaves, and minors mixed together. Women with slaves are forbidden because of frivolity. Minors with slaves are forbidden because of...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reads the משנה as forbidding mixed groups only. A group of only women is still allowed. He starts to explain why each mixture is a problem, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women together with slaves could lead to improper, light-headed behavior. Minors together with slaves also has a problem, but that reason is cut off here. Since only mixed groups are forbidden, רבא's 'women by themselves' reading still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Frivolity; improper, light-headed behavior
Because of

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
(it means) women and slaves and minors (mixed together).
Women and slaves: because of frivolity,
minors and slaves: because of...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the משנה in a narrower way (mixed groups only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids a group of only women, only slaves, or only minors.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids only mixed groups, so a group of only women is allowed.
